chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, who said:

I wrote to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'I am your ransom, grape juice turns into wine, so vinegar and something that changes it are poured over it until it becomes vinegar.' He said: 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine if wine has turned into vinegar?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of *istihlak* (transformation), ruling that adding vinegar and a changing agent to wine effectively removes its intoxicating nature, rendering the resulting vinegar permissible (*halal*). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the mere presence of alcohol and the state of *khamr* (intoxicant), emphasizing that the legal status changes once the primary characteristic of intoxication is nullified through a valid process. The narration highlights the practical application of purification principles in daily life, ensuring that products derived from wine do not remain prohibited if their essential quality is altered.
